title: IBM adds governed agent identities and short-lived credentials
dek: Agent Identity and HashiCorp Vault address delegated authority, revocation and visibility for AI agents operating across business systems.
evidence: IBM product announcement; feature availability varies by component
takeaway: Model each agent as a distinct principal with scoped, expiring credentials, not a shared service account.

sections.title: Architecture

bullets.detail: IBM Agent Identity records agent ownership and delegated authority. Vault applies machine-identity credential controls, including short-lived access, rotation and revocation.
IBM also describes agent discovery, sandbox isolation, evaluation and an NVIDIA OpenShell integration. Some capabilities are generally available while others remain in preview.

paragraphs: Identity layer: IBM Agent Identity records agent ownership and delegated authority. Vault applies machine-identity credential controls, including short-lived access, rotation and revocation.

sections.title: Control gaps

bullets.detail: An agent identity is useful only when all tools validate that principal and its delegated scope at execution time; possession of a token is not sufficient evidence of user intent.
Simulate expired/revoked tokens, cross-agent delegation, tool chaining and partial failures; measure which actions remain possible after rights are removed.
